evidence: Outbox responses are generation-checked against SSE/reset state; regressions cover delayed month and mutation responses across reset.
impact: A stale HTTP response could overwrite newer canonical state or resurrect removed data.
recommendation: Invalidate asynchronous work at lifecycle and SSE boundaries; reconcile from canonical bootstrap after a crossed boundary.
risk: Data convergence failure after reconnect/reset.
validation: Final Node 22 app Vitest: 24 files and 108 tests passed; targeted reset/outbox cases passed.

evidence: Permanent conflicts remove only affected optimistic rows and authoritative reset replaces the working set while preserving valid history/activity/summary projections.
impact: Broad cleanup could discard unrelated downloaded history or leave a poisoned optimistic row.
recommendation: Use targeted discard IDs and an authoritative bootstrap boundary.
risk: Offline data loss or persistent false UI state.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest passed permanent-conflict and authoritative-reset regressions.

evidence: Every async 401 path enters one sticky pairing-expired pause; late successes and reconciliation cannot silently re-pair.
impact: Partial 401 handling could retry unauthorized work or present false synchronization.
recommendation: Centralize pairing expiry and guard all reconnect/mutation/read completions.
risk: Authentication confusion and repeated unauthorized traffic.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest passed existing-cursor, late-success, reconciliation, online-only and probe 401 cases.

evidence: Only the four specified history fallback prefixes use runtime caching; bootstrap and settings are explicitly excluded.
impact: Caching authoritative runtime responses could serve stale identity/settings/bootstrap state.
recommendation: Keep the service-worker allowlist explicit and regression-tested.
risk: Stale authoritative state while online or after reset.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest cache-policy case and final production PWA E2E passed; identical double builds produced the same service-worker hash.

evidence: Offline resume restores the persisted journal timezone/day and queued captures retain the frozen base date intent.
impact: A capture resumed after midnight could silently move to another day.
recommendation: Persist and replay explicit date intent rather than recomputing from wall time.
risk: Incorrect journal dates after offline rollover.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest passed lifecycle and date-intent suites.

evidence: Shutdown flushes a pending draft snapshot and clears outbox, reconnect, assistant-burst, SSE and lifecycle work.
impact: Unmounted work could mutate new state or lose the last draft.
recommendation: Make teardown generation-aware and drain/clear every delayed task.
risk: Lost drafts and cross-lifecycle races.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest passed draft-flush, pending-load and timer shutdown cases.

evidence: Summary tombstones fall back to the greatest loaded summary and then refresh canonical latest state.
impact: Deleting or replacing the latest Summary could leave a stale or empty month projection.
recommendation: Maintain month projections and canonical latest separately, then reconcile.
risk: Incorrect weekly-summary state after SSE changes.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest summary tombstone/fallback cases passed.

evidence: The viewport controller ignores a transient zero-height visual viewport and resets on focus, resume, page-show and orientation changes.
impact: iOS keyboard/orientation events could collapse the application to zero height.
recommendation: Reject invalid viewport samples and force a resume recalculation.
risk: Unusable PWA viewport until reload.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest viewport regression suite passed; physical-device behavior is handed off in RV-043.

evidence: Entry mutations reindex only touched date/collection buckets; a 10,000-row fixture exercises a localized update.
impact: Rebuilding all client indexes on every capture grows linearly with the downloaded journal.
recommendation: Preserve structural sharing and update only touched buckets.
risk: Capture-frame regression as local history grows.
validation: Node 22 app Vitest passed the large localized-index regression.

evidence: The crash-consistent mirror remains one IndexedDB record, but structured cloning is deferred off the synchronous capture path and writes are serialized; a 10,000-entry record round-trips atomically.
impact: Whole-mirror persistence has scale cost, while splitting stores would weaken atomic outbox/mirror durability.
recommendation: Keep the simpler atomic record until measured thresholds fail; retain the 10,000-entry regression.
risk: Accepted memory/write amplification at very large local histories.
validation: Sealed Node 22 benchmark passed: optimistic p95 0.6ms <16ms, committed capture 1.465ms <100ms, MCP read 2.29ms <300ms.

evidence: REST/MCP adapters use stable tuple-keyset SQL pages; same-timestamp and large fixtures assert one bounded SELECT per page without skips.
impact: Materializing an offset-scanned result set can grow memory and query work without bound.
recommendation: Page in SQL using deterministic tuple cursors.
risk: Latency and memory growth on large journals.
validation: Final Node 22 server Vitest passed 17 files/133 tests and integration passed 3 files/30 tests.

evidence: The collection resource deliberately returns the complete collection required by MCP-16, but obtains it in bounded 100-row SQL pages.
impact: The final JSON resource can still be large even though database query memory is bounded.
recommendation: Keep the v1 resource contract; revisit a versioned paged resource only if operational measurements require it.
risk: Accepted response-size growth for unusually large collections.
validation: Bounded-query integration regression passed; NFR benchmark passed. Contract change deferred absent a measured failure.

evidence: Activity revert eligibility batches snapshot lookups by entity rather than issuing one query per snapshot; a >500 same-timestamp fixture preserves ordering and completeness.
impact: N+1 reads could make Review latency proportional to snapshot count.
recommendation: Batch entity reads and compute comparisons in memory.
risk: Review endpoint performance degradation.
validation: Final Node 22 integration suite passed 3 files/30 tests.

evidence: The browser imports the explicit app-safe contract and the Vite production guard rejects any server-only MCP contract in emitted chunks.
impact: MCP/server-only schema leakage couples bundle layout and expands the browser surface.
recommendation: Expose a browser-safe contract entrypoint and enforce it at bundle time.
risk: Bundle bloat and accidental server API coupling.
validation: Node 22 app build, Vite guard tests and final clean release build passed.

evidence: Reserved /api and /mcp paths retain route-appropriate JSON 404/body errors and never fall through to the SPA.
impact: Malformed or unknown API traffic could be misclassified or return the app shell.
recommendation: Classify client JSON failures narrowly and reserve both prefixes.
risk: Protocol ambiguity and false-success HTML responses.
validation: Final Node 22 HTTP/MCP integration cases passed within 3 files/30 tests.

evidence: Host and Origin validation compare scheme-aware allowed origins; pairing emits the hardened device cookie.
impact: Authority-only Origin checks can accept the wrong scheme or origin form.
recommendation: Compare normalized origins and fail closed on Host/Origin mismatch.
risk: Cross-origin mutation or pairing exposure.
validation: Node 22 real-server Host/Origin/pairing integration passed.

evidence: Unknown/untrusted tool names are not interpolated into content-bearing logs; mixed JSON-RPC batch rejections are audited once per call.
impact: Attacker-controlled tool text could enter operator logs or duplicate audits.
recommendation: Log fixed operation metadata and redact request content.
risk: Sensitive-content leakage and misleading audit counts.
validation: Node 22 mixed-batch/content-free audit integration passed.

evidence: A capacity-512 session event store replays missed resource-list changes exactly once; notifier storms coalesce and close the stream after delivery.
impact: A reconnect could miss or duplicate resource-list changes.
recommendation: Assign event IDs, replay within a bounded session journal and close notification streams deterministically.
risk: MCP client state divergence.
validation: Node 22 unit race tests and real-transport reconnect integration passed.

evidence: add_entry returns the canonical entry-or-summary union and the server exposes exactly seven tools with the documented annotations.
impact: A weaker output schema can reject legitimate summary filing or drift from the domain.
recommendation: Share one canonical union at the MCP boundary and assert the exact inventory.
risk: Client schema failure and contract drift.
validation: Node 22 contract and seven-tool transport tests passed.

evidence: Each SSE client has a maximum buffered-byte budget and is disconnected on backpressure before later mutations can grow its queue.
impact: A paused client could retain unbounded server memory.
recommendation: Bound per-client buffering and force cursor-based replay after disconnect.
risk: Denial of service and process exhaustion.
validation: Node 22 unit test passed; independent 100,000-notification paused-client probe completed near flat heap and retained only one coalesced event.

evidence: Replay is session-local and capped at 512; no keepalive frames are sent, and list-change streams close after notification so clients reconnect with Last-Event-ID.
impact: This differs from an indefinitely open heartbeat stream but removes an otherwise unsafe backpressure path.
recommendation: Retain the bounded reconnect design and exact-once transport tests.
risk: Accepted reconnect overhead and replay-window limit.
validation: Exact-once reconnect, coalescing and SDK transport tests passed; no correctness finding remains.

evidence: A private SQLite-backed writer lease rejects a concurrent process, detects dead/PID-reused owners and releases only its own token.
impact: Two live writers can split journal state or corrupt assumptions around WAL/maintenance.
recommendation: Acquire the lease before opening the writable runtime and release it last.
risk: Data corruption or lost writes.
validation: Node 22 process-level kill/recovery and metadata tests passed.

evidence: Shutdown quiesces ingress first, cancels/drains active backup work, uses a 250ms best-effort WAL checkpoint and releases storage/lease; a real external reader pins WAL in the process test.
impact: A 5s SQLite busy timeout or active backup could make SIGTERM miss launchd's lifecycle budget.
recommendation: Bound checkpoint time, make backups abortable and preserve recoverable WAL when busy.
risk: Forced termination during shutdown and delayed recovery.
validation: Node 22 real-process held-reader and active-SSE shutdown tests passed within the five-second contract.

evidence: A verified temporary snapshot is prepared before atomic replacement; corrupt regular files are hard-linked to quarantine, corrupt symlinks are copied without following targets, and replacement rollback removes quarantine safely.
impact: Moving the corrupt canonical first leaves a missing-backup gap; following a symlink could modify an external target.
recommendation: Verify before replace and preserve the old inode/link without removing the canonical path.
risk: Loss of the last backup or external-file mutation.
validation: Node 22 corrupt-file, corrupt-symlink and swapped-directory backup tests passed.

evidence: Backup due-ness uses the latest due 03:30 date, ignores future-dated snapshots, and maintenance tracks the last attempted schedule rather than a pre-due clock tick.
impact: A restart before 03:30 followed by a later tick could skip the day's backup; future files could suppress it.
recommendation: Calculate the latest due calendar date in the configured timezone and retry corrupt/missing schedules.
risk: Silent gaps in daily recovery points.
validation: Node 22 02:00-to-04:00 catch-up and future-snapshot regressions passed.

evidence: Numbered SQL migrations ship with the compiled CLI; startup rejects unknown, non-contiguous or checksum-drifted history and takes a verified online pre-migration backup.
impact: Source/build drift or accepting a future schema can run incompatible code against the database.
recommendation: Validate a contiguous known migration prefix and package the SQL assets.
risk: Schema corruption or incompatible downgrade.
validation: Node 22 migration, future-history and compiled-CLI asset tests passed.

evidence: Export runs all table reads inside one SQLite read transaction and validates JournalExportV1; import validates cross-references, month collection rules and saved-summary references before commit.
impact: Concurrent writes can produce a torn export; invalid references can create unrecoverable imported state.
recommendation: Snapshot and schema-validate export; preflight all referential invariants on import.
risk: Non-lossless portability or corrupt imported journal.
validation: Node 22 round-trip, write-between-reads and broken-reference tests passed.

evidence: Saving a Summary repairs a soft-deleted saved note rather than reusing an invalid deleted row; rewrite/relink remains revision-checked.
impact: A Summary could point at a deleted entry and appear saved when no visible note exists.
recommendation: Relink or recreate the saved note inside the Summary transaction.
risk: Broken Summary lifecycle and false UI status.
validation: Node 22 deleted-summary-note regression passed.

evidence: Search normalizes NFC and uses a deterministic Unicode lower function for permissive substring matching in addition to FTS candidates.
impact: ASCII-only lowercasing misses valid case-insensitive Unicode matches.
recommendation: Use Unicode-aware normalization/lowercasing at the SQL fallback boundary.
risk: Incorrect search results for non-ASCII journal text.
validation: Node 22 Unicode substring regression passed.

evidence: Existing data/backup/log directories must already be real, current-user-owned and owner-private; missing dedicated directories/files are created 0700/0600 without chmod of broad existing paths.
impact: A configuration typo could chmod a shared directory or expose database/WAL/lease material.
recommendation: Refuse broad, symlinked, foreign-owned or permissive existing targets; harden only newly created app paths and private files.
risk: Host permission damage or journal disclosure.
validation: Node 22 broad-directory, symlink and umask file-mode regressions passed.

evidence: check/export/backup use readonly fileMustExist connections with migrations disabled; output canonicalization rejects database, WAL/SHM, backups, logs, hardlinks and symlink aliases.
impact: A supposedly safe inspection could create/migrate/checkpoint an empty database or overwrite a control file.
recommendation: Separate readonly CLI construction and reject all canonical control-path aliases before writing.
risk: Unexpected production mutation or data overwrite.
validation: Node 22 missing/table-less DB, live-writer and output-alias tests passed.

evidence: The installer validates executable Node/regular CLI, takes a disjoint private install lock, lints a temporary plist, atomically replaces, verifies launchctl adoption and explicitly reports rollback cleanup failures.
impact: Concurrent or partial launchd installation can leave the old job stopped, a bad plist installed or ownership ambiguous.
recommendation: Serialize install, validate before bootout, restore exact prior plist/job and fail on incomplete cleanup.
risk: Service outage or adoption of the wrong runtime.
validation: Node 22 install-service suite passed atomic replace, failure injection, concurrent lock and rollback cases.

evidence: Runtime composition owns partially created database/domain/Vite/application values and attempts every cleanup on startup failure; normal close is idempotent.
impact: A dynamic-import or constructor failure could leak the lease, database or Vite server.
recommendation: Create resources inside one cleanup boundary and preserve the original error while best-effort closing all acquired resources.
risk: Stuck writer lease and failed restart.
validation: Node 22 full server suite passed including runtime shutdown/startup paths.

evidence: Runtime support is exactly Node 22.19.x, CI enables forbidOnly/fail-on-flaky behavior, and axe runs every primary view plus Assistant access at narrow and wide viewports.
impact: Overbroad Node support or partial/flaky browser gates can certify an untested release.
recommendation: Pin the release runtime and make full accessibility/flaky detection release-blocking.
risk: False green release on another ABI/runtime or untested view.
validation: Final clean Node 22.19.0 preparation passed; CI-mode Playwright completed 31 tests with 6 intentional project-inapplicable skips.

evidence: Preparation clean-installs/tests/benchmarks before sealing exact dirty-tree bytes/modes/toolchain; staging verifies hashes, rejects toolchain drift, installs production dependencies and makes the tree immutable.
impact: Deploying from a mutable checkout or rebuilding after browser tests can run bytes that were never verified.
recommendation: Archive the browser-tested bundle into a manifest-bound immutable stage and execute staged helpers thereafter.
risk: Unreviewed or ABI-incompatible production deployment.
validation: All 88/88 release-tool tests passed; final promotion revalidated immutable deployed-tree SHA 72b16666b885f3d38842a185488a3fff77b1581ef3b3b7767f0f2a7623917560 and the exact manifest/archive hashes.

evidence: Cutover is mode-aware and self-restoring; verifiers compare the complete Serve config, protect exact :443, require only the :5178 delta, one launchd PID/listener, health version and exact served asset bytes.
impact: A weak cutover can overwrite unrelated Serve handlers or claim success while old bytes/PID still serve.
recommendation: Capture exact pre-state, mutate only owned surfaces, verify adoption and restore exact pre-state on failure.
risk: Collateral service outage or false deployment success.
validation: Live rehearsal and final cutover passed: exact launchd PID/listener and asset adoption were proved, :443 was unchanged and the complete Serve comparison found zero collateral change.

evidence: Promotion requires a unique fresh 0600 online backup restored through staged check/export, a machine-green release ledger and immutable evidence before atomically moving current-release.
impact: A same-day reused backup or narrative-only checklist can allow promotion without recoverability proof.
recommendation: Bind restore-tested backup and every acceptance result to the release context and revalidate at promotion.
risk: Unrecoverable release or unsupported compliance claim.
validation: A unique mode-0600 backup passed quick_check, staged CLI check and export validation; the 83-gate ledger was revalidated during atomic promotion.

evidence: Lifecycle evidence binds distinct initial, post-SIGTERM and post-SIGKILL PIDs, signals, durations and fresh runtime/asset proofs; promotion rejects incoherent identity.
impact: A restart command can report success while the old process remains or recovery exceeds five seconds.
recommendation: Target exact PIDs and verify a distinct healthy replacement after each signal.
risk: Unproven crash recovery.
validation: Final launchd lifecycle evidence passed: SIGTERM replaced PID 19546 with 19790 in 62.727ms; SIGKILL replaced PID 19790 with 20167 in 62.745ms; both replacements were healthy and exact-release-bound.

evidence: Rollback validates context/pointer/evidence before mutation; a successful rollback leaves terminal evidence/lock and the same context cannot roll back again or promote.
impact: Reusing a terminal context can mutate a newer installation or create conflicting ownership claims.
recommendation: Serialize terminal operations and reject rollback/promotion after terminal evidence.
risk: Rollback of the wrong release or split promotion ownership.
validation: Live first-install apply/verify/rollback rehearsal restored the exact Serve baseline and wrote terminal ownership evidence; final promotion then wrote its own terminal lock and atomic pointer evidence.

evidence: Architecture inventory, exact Node/Tailnet surface and fail-closed operator flow now match the implemented packages and release helpers.
impact: Stale docs can direct operators to unsafe manual deployment or nonexistent layout.
recommendation: Treat specs/runbook as release-bound contract and validate referenced commands/files.
risk: Operator error and unsupported release claims.
validation: The final release preparation sealed these exact documentation and source bytes into the immutable tree.

evidence: P2 advanced migration shortcuts and multi-journal/archive/Markdown export are explicitly excluded; only versioned lossless JSON portability remains included.
impact: Treating deferred P2 as an implementation gap would expand scope and destabilize v1.
recommendation: Record the exclusion in the ledger while testing DM-20 JSON portability.
risk: Accepted deferred functionality, not a defect.
validation: Domain JSON round-trip tests passed; ledger rows remain P2 EXCLUDED.

evidence: The product intentionally has exactly seven MCP tools, five automatic writes, two reads, an empty compatibility proposals resource and no proposal queue or installed scheduler.
impact: Adding a proposal system or scheduler would contradict the approved product boundary.
recommendation: Keep automation explicit in the MCP contract and weekly skill while leaving scheduling to the invoking agent.
risk: Accepted product decision.
validation: Exact-seven transport test and process/release inspection gate cover this boundary.

evidence: Seven physical-iPhone standalone checks are explicitly assigned to the owner; no simulator/desktop result is represented as device certification.
impact: Claiming a physical pass without a named device/iOS/account is false evidence.
recommendation: Create release-bound DEVICE HANDOFF evidence with assignee, checklist reference and notes; accept PASS only with device provenance.
risk: Residual physical-device compatibility remains owner-verified.
validation: Final device evidence is release-bound, references SPEC-05 section 8, assigns all seven checks to Robert and explicitly claims no device pass.

evidence: Topmost dialogs trap Tab/Shift-Tab from panel or background, preserve focus on rerender and restore the opener on close.
impact: Keyboard focus could escape behind a modal or be stolen after a late route render.
recommendation: Own a dialog stack and stable focus lifecycle; avoid refocusing the day view after first selection.
risk: Keyboard and screen-reader navigation failure.
validation: Node 22 component tests passed; production Playwright focus scenario passed in the implementation gate.

evidence: The visual calendar is an accurately labelled group of day buttons rather than an incomplete ARIA grid; blank cells are hidden.
impact: A partial grid pattern announces misleading row/column semantics.
recommendation: Use native buttons with complete labels unless full keyboard-grid interaction is implemented.
risk: Confusing assistive-technology navigation.
validation: Node 22 MonthView semantics tests passed.

evidence: Migration waits for each mutation, announces pending/failure/next state and focuses the next task only after success.
impact: Announcing progress before commit can tell assistive users an action succeeded when it failed.
recommendation: Await the operation before advancing the queue and live region.
risk: False completion feedback.
validation: Node 22 MigrationDialog async/failure tests passed.

evidence: Calendar navigation/day cells, search input and mobile/coarse interactive controls retain at least 40px hit targets down to 320px.
impact: Compressed calendar/search controls could fall below the approved mobile target.
recommendation: Give key controls explicit min dimensions and audit computed boxes at narrow widths.
risk: Touch usability and WCAG target-size failure.
validation: Final app unit suite and CI-mode Playwright responsive audit passed at narrow widths.

evidence: Remote failure is labeled 'Search unavailable' and downloaded-only matches/empty state are distinguished from authoritative no results.
impact: An offline/failed search looked like a real empty journal result.
recommendation: Track remote search status separately from result count.
risk: User makes decisions from incomplete data.
validation: Node 22 SearchDialog failure regression passed.

evidence: Migrated/cancelled actionable entries expose no illegal toggle, migration, drop or filing controls; non-actionable entries retain legal filing.
impact: Terminal tasks could still be mutated through an unsupported action.
recommendation: Derive available controls from canonical type/state legality.
risk: Domain validation errors and misleading controls.
validation: Node 22 state-table component regressions passed.

evidence: Control borders/focus rings use corrected AA tokens and safe-area content inset is applied once in the main pane; visual viewport height excludes transient keyboard space.
impact: Low-contrast focus indicators or double top inset reduce accessibility and usable space.
recommendation: Centralize contrast tokens and separate background safe-area paint from content padding.
risk: WCAG failure or clipped mobile layout.
validation: Final Node 22 app tests, axe scenarios and 48-shot visual release audit passed with zero overflow or dimension mismatches.

evidence: Yesterday is computed as a calendar-key predecessor at UTC noon rather than subtracting 24 local hours.
impact: DST transitions can mislabel activity as Yesterday.
recommendation: Operate on calendar keys, not elapsed milliseconds in the display timezone.
risk: Incorrect activity grouping around DST.
validation: Node 22 date regression suite passed.

evidence: Owner entry creation resolves today/tomorrow from the request's frozen baseToday even when server wall time has crossed midnight; absolute intent stays exact.
impact: Rebasing a queued date intent at sync time can file an offline entry on a different journal day.
recommendation: Treat the client-captured date context as canonical after schema validation and make replay hash the full request.
risk: Silent date corruption during offline replay.
validation: Final Node 22 server Vitest passed 17 files/133 tests including stale today, tomorrow and absolute intent assertions.

evidence: POST /api/capture uses its explicit frozen dateIntent for persistence while still returning the parser's >tomorrow preview metadata.
impact: Re-parsing >tomorrow when a queued capture finally arrives can override its frozen absolute target and shift the entry twice.
recommendation: Separate parser presentation metadata from the already-captured persistence date intent.
risk: Wrong-day capture after an offline midnight boundary.
validation: Node 22 capture integration asserts parsed dateShift=1 while the committed date remains the frozen absolute date; final full server 17/133 passed.

evidence: Deployed-tree traversal, record sorting and attestation validation share an explicit relational path comparator instead of localeCompare; an identical-fixture regression asserts deterministic mixed-case source ordering.
impact: Locale-sensitive ordering could change the immutable tree digest across hosts without any byte drift.
recommendation: Use one locale-independent comparator for traversal, records and ordering validation.
risk: Host-dependent release identity or false attestation mismatch.
validation: Final release-tool suite passed 88/88; deployed-tree evidence records 6,040 paths and SHA 72b16666b885f3d38842a185488a3fff77b1581ef3b3b7767f0f2a7623917560, revalidated at promotion.

evidence: Lifecycle opens the stable owner-private nofollow global release lock, acquires lockf before evidence absence, and holds it through terminal validation, both signals, runtime/tree checks and atomic evidence commit.
impact: Lifecycle could interleave with cutover or promotion and signal or attest a runtime whose ownership changed mid-operation.
recommendation: Serialize every release lifecycle operation on the same stable lock and verify its inode before close.
risk: Cross-operation release corruption or false lifecycle proof.
validation: Final release-tool suite passed 88/88 with ordering and contention assertions; final lifecycle evidence records distinct healthy PID recovery in 62.727ms and 62.745ms.

evidence: Atomic-evidence recovery classifies every owner before mutation, preserves a committed two-link winner, removes dead unpublished losers, finalizes the winner and fails closed if any losing owner is live.
impact: A crash with winner and loser residue could block promotion forever or delete the committed evidence bytes.
recommendation: Recover mixed states by inode/link identity with retry-safe unlinks and a final directory fsync; never guess around live owners.
risk: Lost or ambiguous terminal release evidence.
validation: Final release-tool suite passed 88/88, including committed-winner/dead-loser recovery and live-loser fail-closed tests; final promotion evidence and terminal marker committed successfully.

evidence: UTC release-stamp components are kept as strings, while zsh file-mode arithmetic uses explicit base-8 literals; the helper smoke test rejects unsafe implicit leading-zero mode expressions.
impact: Timestamp components containing 08/09 or ambiguous leading-zero mode literals can be parsed as invalid octal or evaluated differently by zsh.
recommendation: Construct release stamps without numeric coercion and use explicit radix notation for octal guards.
risk: Release preparation or ownership validation fails only at particular dates or modes.
validation: Final release-tool suite passed 88/88; final stamp 20260731T182812Z-88ff6fa9bc5d-14233 was prepared and promoted with the guarded helpers.

evidence: Upgrade preflight scopes lsof to the exact launchd PID and TCP 5178, requires one loopback listener, then re-reads launchd PID/cwd to prevent generation drift; the harness injects unrelated same-port PIDs.
impact: A host-wide :5178 query can count Tailscale IPNExtension sockets and falsely reject or misattribute the Journal listener.
recommendation: Intersect listener inspection with the owned launchd PID and revalidate that process generation after inspection.
risk: False cutover failure or listener-ownership claim.
validation: Final release-tool suite passed 88/88; cutover and promotion evidence bind PID 20167 to only 127.0.0.1:5178 while preserving the complete Serve configuration.

evidence: After bootout, installer and staged cutover require two separated launchctl not-found observations before same-label bootstrap; rollback cleanup repeats the bounded confirmation and refuses bootstrap when absence is unproved.
impact: Asynchronous launchd deregistration can make an immediate bootstrap race the retiring job, including during rollback.
recommendation: Wait for stable label absence after every accepted bootout and before candidate or rollback bootstrap; fail closed on timeout or unexpected status.
risk: Service outage, failed adoption or rollback into an ambiguous launchd state.
validation: Final server suite passed 17 files/133 tests and release tools passed 88/88, covering delayed absence, timeout, unexpected status and restored-old-job rollback; final upgrade cutover and promotion completed.
